This was established by analyzing dispute ticket trends (E-01), billing data indicating more disputes linked to actual than estimated reads (E-04), and AMI read event data showing 1184 disputed estimated bills have AMI reads rejected for high consumption (E-10, E-11), with evidence revisions ER-1 and ER-2 updating interpretations to reflect that the surge is not solely due to low route completion. The planned release scope was to review the validation rule for high consumption targeting DA-RULES, but no release was made because the release gate resulted in a HOLD. The release was held because the release assumes completeness of inputs while DA-RULES completeness is unknown (hold reason: completeness unknown while release assumes completeness: incomplete inputs used by release: ['DA-RULES']) and because Layer 1 verification (safety predicate) was not established (hold reason: safety predicate / verification not established (Layer 1 failed)) as indicated in the release gate result (seq 230). Known limitations include the unknown completeness of DA-RULES and the lack of an established safety predicate/verification; no additional limitations were listed.
